title: 2024 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement: Minh enters the numbers \(1\) through \(81\) into the cells of a \(9 \times 9\) grid in some order. She calculates the product of the numbers in each row and column. What is the least number of rows and columns that could have a product divisible by \(3?\)

solutions.text:
There are \(27\) multiples of \(3\) from \(1\) through \(81\). A row or column has product divisible by \(3\) exactly when it contains at least one of these multiples.

Suppose \(r\) rows and \(c\) columns have products divisible by \(3\). Every multiple of \(3\) must lie in one of those \(r\) rows and also in one of those \(c\) columns, or else it would create another marked row or column. Thus the \(27\) multiples must fit in the \(rc\) intersection cells. If \(r+c\le10\), then \(rc\le25\), which is too small. So at least \(11\) rows and columns are needed.

This can be done by placing \(25\) multiples of \(3\) in a \(5\times5\) block, then placing the remaining \(2\) multiples in a sixth column within two of those same rows. Then exactly \(5\) rows and \(6\) columns are marked, for a total of \(11\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Only multiples of \(3\) make a row or column product divisible by \(3\)
Cover the \(27\) multiples of \(3\) using as few rows and columns as possible
